\section*{Question 3}

A car is traveling on a straight road with velocity 55 ft /sec at time \(t=0\). For \(0 \leq t \leq 18\) seconds, the car's acceleration \(a(t)\), in \(\mathrm{ft} / \mathrm{sec}^{2}\), is the piecewise linear function defined by the graph above.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Is the velocity of the car increasing at \(t=2\) seconds? Why or why not?
\item[(b)] At what time in the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 18\), other than \(t=0\), is the velocity of the car 55 ft/sec? Why?
\item[(c)] On the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 18\), what is the car's absolute maximum velocity, in ft/sec, and at what time does it occur? Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] At what times in the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 18\), if any, is the car's velocity equal to zero? Justify your answer.
\item[(a)] Since \(v^{\prime}(2)=a(2)\) and \(a(2)=15>0\), the velocity is increasing at \(t=2\).
\item[(b)] At time \(t=12\) because
\[
v(12)-v(0)=\int_{0}^{12} a(t) d t=0
\]
\item[(c)] The absolute maximum velocity is 115 ft/sec at \(t=6\).
The absolute maximum must occur at \(t=6\) or at an endpoint.
\[
\begin{aligned}
& v(6)=55+\int_{0}^{6} a(t) d t \\
& \quad=55+2(15)+\frac{1}{2}(4)(15)=115>v(0) \\
& \int_{6}^{18} a(t) d t<0 \text { so } v(18)<v(6)
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] The car's velocity is never equal to 0. The absolute minimum occurs at \(t=16\) where
\[
v(16)=115+\int_{6}^{16} a(t) d t=115-105=10>0
\]
\end{itemize}

1 : answer and reason
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: t=12 \\ 1: \text { reason }\end{array}\right.\)
\(4:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: t=6 \\ 1: \text { absolute maximum velocity } \\ 1: \text { identifies } t=6 \text { and } \\ t=18 \text { as candidates } \\ \text { or } \\ \text { indicates that } v \text { increases, } \\ \text { decreases, then increases } \\ 1: \text { eliminates } t=18\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { answer } \\ 1: \text { reason }\end{array}\right.\)
